newsitem.title: USA: 17-year-old arrested in slaying of Seattle family.
newsitem.headline: 17-year-old arrested in slaying of Seattle family.

text.p: A 17-year-old boy was arrested in the slayings of a family of four and has confessed to involvement in a crime that has shocked residents in this upscale Seattle suburb, police said Friday.
Police said they expected to charge the youth, an acquaintance of the family's, with four counts of first-degree murder.
The boy, whose name was not immediately released, was being held in a juvenile facility while prosecutors decided whether to try him as an adult.

William Wilson, 52, his wife, Rosalie, 46, and their daughter Julia, 17, were found stabbed and bludgeoned to death in their house Sunday, shortly after the body of their other daughter, Kimberly, 20, was found strangled in a nearby park.

The suspect, who came to know the family as an acquaintance of Kimberly's, was first questioned Monday and then was arrested late Thursday as police were trying to calm fears at a neighbourhood meeting with several hundred people.
The suspect lived in Bellevue about two miles (three km) from the victims and had a job in construction, police said.
"He has cooperated to the point where he has admitted his involvement in this homicide," interim Police Chief Garney Arcand said at a news conference.
Arcand declined to comment on motive, although police said the slaying was not random, not drug-related and not a professional "hit." Detectives said the murder weapons had not been recovered.
The quadruple homicide was Bellevue's worst ever. The town of 90,000 people lies across Lake Washington from Seattle. It had only three homicides in all of 1996.
